prompt:
The same Berlin bicycle lane, seen from the side, wide, vertical frame. The
young man is exactly where the second reference photograph puts him: OUT IN
THE MIDDLE OF THE RED STRIP, both white leather sneakers flat on the red
paint with a clear stretch of red on either side of him, the grey pavement
slabs far away at the left edge of the frame. He wears the navy blue polo
shirt and beige chinos and he has stopped walking and turned to his right to
face the other man. Keep him on the red paint. On the right the heavy-set grey-bearded man from the first
reference photograph -- about fifty, broad-shouldered, a dark grey cycling
helmet, thin rimless glasses, a BRIGHT YELLOW waterproof jacket -- has
stopped his dark grey bicycle across the lane and stands over it with one
foot flat on the ground, facing him, one hand on the handlebars. He is a
head shorter and much broader than the young man. There is a pace of empty red strip between them. BEYOND THEM, further down the lane, the same crossing is in
view: a pedestrian traffic light on a grey pole at the kerb, small with
distance, the zebra crossing beside it. The pale cream facade with its tall
stone-framed windows runs along behind, with three or four black city
bicycles leaning against the wall, well spaced. The lane is clear in both directions. Grey
pavement slabs to the left, a granite kerb. Daylight, overcast and flat.
